benchmarks.task_description:
Loadpoint: synchronize SoC estimator access

follows up #35764

API callers like the plan endpoints read the SoC estimator via `GetPlanRequiredDuration` while the control loop mutates it in `publishSocAndRange`, and `SetVehicle` replaces the estimator pointer from the API goroutine. Both were unsynchronized.

- `Estimator` guards its state with an internal mutex, including the session `Reset`
- the estimator pointer is guarded by the vehicle mutex and swapped together with the active vehicle, so vehicle and estimator always match
- readers obtain vehicle and estimator as one consistent snapshot
- plan duration no longer dereferences a vehicle that was removed concurrently

fix: use a ref for the catalogue's stale-response guard

Closes #151

## What

`web/src/pages/Catalogue.tsx` — the first effect's stale-response guard moves from a local
`let cancelled` to a component-scope `useRef<boolean>`. Behaviour is unchanged: the ref is
reset before each load and set in the cleanup, so a superseded `kind`/`token` answer is still
ignored.

## Why

The web tooling bump in #139 raises `oxlint` 1.89 → 1.91, which turns on `react(immutability)`
(category `correctness`, set to `error`) and fails `make web_check` on this one site. This fix
lets #139 merge without leaving `dev`'s web gate red. See #151.

## Verification

- [x] `make check` — exit 0 (gofmt, vet, test, build)
- [x] `make web_check` — exit 0 under oxlint 1.89.0 (current `dev`)
- [x] `make build` — exit 0 (with Node 24.22.1 on PATH)
- Untested packages/areas touched: `web/src/pages/Catalogue.tsx` has no automated test (the
  `web` Go package test is the embed test). Verified by the web gate and by inspecting the diff.
- Also verified under oxlint **1.91.0** (the version #139 brings): `oxlint` exit 0 (only the
  pre-existing `TemplateDetail.tsx` warning remains) and `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

## Notes

- Only the flagged effect changes. The identical `cancelled` pattern in the second `Catalogue`
  effect, `Files.tsx` and `TemplateDetail.tsx` is **not** flagged by oxlint 1.91.0, so it is
  left untouched to keep the diff minimal. If a later oxlint version starts flagging those,
  they get the same treatment.

benchmarks.task_description:
websites: find wp-config.php one level above the WordPress folder

Closes stefanpejcic/OpenPanel#1298

wp-admin auto-login from OpenAdmin failed with `wp-config.php not found` on sites that move wp-config.php out of the web root, because it only looked in the docroot.

This builds on #19 and adds the changes asked for in its review:

- the parent folder's wp-config.php is used only when that folder has no `wp-settings.php`, like `wp-load.php` does, so it never picks up another WordPress install's config
- it never looks outside the user's html volume (exact match or `htmlData + "/"`, so a sibling like `_data2` doesn't count)
- English one-line comments, with tests for the moved config, docroot config winning, parent with its own `wp-settings.php` (still "not found"), and a docroot at the volume root

Tested on a real server: moved `wp-config.php` of a `example.org/test` WordPress one folder up, the site kept working, OpenAdmin's login link failed before the fix and logged into wp-admin after it (token rejected on reuse).

The user panel had the same bug, fixed in stefanpejcic/OpenPanel (linked from the issue).

wordpress: find wp-config.php one level above the WordPress folder

Refs #1298

WP Manager login and the users list had the same problem as OpenAdmin's auto-login: with wp-config.php moved out of the web root they returned `wp-config.php not found`, even though WordPress itself loads it from the parent folder.

`getWPConfigDBInfo` now looks where `wp-load.php` does: the parent folder is used only when it has no `wp-settings.php` of its own, and never outside the user's html volume. Reads still go through `tenantfs`.

The OpenAdmin side is https://github.com/stefanpejcic/openadmin/pull/22.

Tested on a real server with a subfolder WordPress whose config was moved one level up: login and users list failed before, and found the config and the administrator after.

Also bumps `klauspost/compress` to v1.20.2 in a separate commit, because govulncheck started failing on GO-2026-6865 (reached through the mongo driver). Happy to drop it if you'd rather bump it on main.

fix(web): keep the Out of date chip's icon and words in one box

Closes #3250

## What and why

The Out of date chip's own `flex-wrap: wrap` stacked its icon above its words once the attribute cluster was narrower than both, and the `nowrap` words then ran past the capped box. It happens from the desktop layout (780px) up, when a CI pill with counts fills the status cell (measured in the issue). The phone layout was never affected.

- `.attr-chip` no longer wraps, so icon and words stay on one line.
- `.attr-cluster` is never narrower than its widest chip (`min-width: min-content`), and `.state-group` wraps, so the cluster drops under the CI slot when it doesn't fit beside it. Nothing is clipped.
- The Forgejo "Scheduled on Forgejo" chip keeps its wrap, since its note sits on a second line by design (`:has(> .pill-note)`).

Colours are untouched; `attr-chip-contrast.test.ts` passes. The new spec runs on both the Bots and Pull requests pages, light and dark, at 390, 820, 1280 and 1935px.

### Summary

The not-found checks looked for *network.NotFoundError, but the helpers return NotFoundError as a value, so retry_timeout never retried. Check for the value type.

FromNameAndDVSUuid also returned govmomi's *find.NotFoundError, or a plain error when the name only exists on another switch. Return NotFoundError for both so lookups with distributed_virtual_switch_uuid retry too. This means the error message is now "Network <name> not found" instead of the old message naming the specific switch UUID.

Closes #2802

### Type

- [x] `fix`: Bug Fix
- [ ] `feat`: Feature or Enhancement
- [ ] `docs`: Documentation
- [ ] `refactor`: Refactoring
- [ ] `chore`: Build, Dependencies, Workflows, etc.
- [ ] `other`: Other (Please describe.)

### Breaking Changes?

- [ ] Yes, there are breaking changes.
- [x] No, there are no breaking changes.

### Tests

- [ ] Tests have been added or updated.
- [x] Tests have been completed.

Output:

`make test` and `golangci-lint run` pass.

I don't have a vCenter to run the acceptance tests against, so I tested against vcsim with `retry_timeout = 20`, with
and without this change:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Standard network that never appears | fails after 0s | times out after 20s |
| Standard port group created after 8s | fails after 0s | found after 16s |
| DVS port group (by switch UUID) that never appears | fails after 0s | times out after 20s |
| DVS port group created after 8s | fails after 0s | found after 16s |
| Same name on another switch, created on this one after 8s | fails after 0s | found after 15s |
| Existing DVS port group / standard network | found | found |

### Documentation

- [ ] Documentation has been added or updated.

### Issue References

Closes #2802

### Release Note

```
- `d/vsphere_network`: Fixed `retry_timeout` not waiting for a network that is not found. (#2803)
```

### Additional Information
